definitions.explanation: A snake that produces venom and can deliver it through a bite. In Japan, common venomous snakes include the mamushi (pit viper) and habu.

examples.japanese: {毒蛇|どくへび}に{注意|ちゅうい}。
{山道|やまみち}で{毒蛇|どくへび}に{噛|か}まれた。
examples.english: I was bitten by a venomous snake on the mountain trail.

examples.japanese: マムシは{日本|にほん}で{最|もっと}も{身近|みぢか}な{毒蛇|どくへび}のひとつだ。
examples.english: The mamushi is one of the most commonly encountered venomous snakes in Japan.

notes:
Also read as どくじゃ, though どくへび is the more common reading in everyday speech. Strictly speaking, 'venomous' (injecting toxin via bite) is more accurate than 'poisonous' (toxic when ingested), but {毒蛇|どくへび} covers both in Japanese.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {毒蛇|どくへび}に{噛|か}まれる: to be bitten by a venomous snake
- {毒蛇|どくへび}の{毒|どく}: snake venom
- {毒蛇|どくへび}に{注意|ちゅうい}: warning about venomous snakes

RELATED TERMS:
- マムシ: Japanese pit viper — the most common venomous snake in mainland Japan
- ハブ: habu — a large venomous pit viper found in Okinawa
- {蛇|へび}: snake — the general term
- {毒|どく}: poison, venom
